HE TURNED “NO” INTO “WHAT’S NEXT?” ✈️💡

When 17-year-old student pilot Jack Kirby kept getting turned down for flight-training scholarships, he decided to make the search easier for someone else.

Kirby launched ZeroToSolo, a free web platform designed to connect aspiring aviators with scholarships and accessible training options, according to a November 13 report from General Aviation News.

The reported process starts with a short set of questions about a student’s goals and background, then produces a personalized roadmap. Its scholarship resources include opportunities from organizations such as AOPA, EAA, Women in Aviation International and The Ninety-Nines.

The tool helps people look for opportunities; eligibility, deadlines and award decisions still belong to the individual scholarship providers.

What stands out is the initiative: a student facing a difficult path into aviation built something intended to help the next person along it.

Here’s to young aviators who keep going—and bring others with them. 💛
